newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: EMU hopes boost Portuguese escudo to two-year high.
newsitem.headline: EMU hopes boost Portuguese escudo to two-year high.

text.p: Growing confidence that Portugal will qualify for the European Union's single currency in the first wave drove the escudo to a two-year high on Wednesday, dealer said.
"The latest news about the Portuguese economy is positive and points to Portugal being ready to form part of the first group (moving to monetary union)," said one market analyst.
"This is favouring the escudo," he said, noting that the decline in money market yields was being seen as a reflection of this mounting confidence.

The escudo was trading at 101.13/17 to the German mark at 1355 GMT against its opening 101.53/58, as most European currencies advanced against the mark. But it was also firmer on the peseta, rising to 120.30 to the Spanish unit from 120.70 in early trade.
"Mark-escudo is falling steadily because there is a lot of marks being offered abroad," said Jorge Farrajota of Siemca-Sociedade Mediadora de Capitais.
Traders said the next target for the currency was 101.00.
Dealers said the bulk of the mark-escudo pressure came out of London, with Madrid and Paris following its lead.
"The escudo is beginning to be seen in a different light. People are taking a positive view on the economy," said the market analyst who asked not to be named.

The analyst said assurances that the 1997 budget would be passed when it comes before parliament later this month, plus Portugal's high degree of political stability and the coincidence of views in the two main political parties on the need to join monetary union lay behind the new confidence.
"It is all about confidence in the Portuguese economy. It is a movement that has been taking shape over the past couple of weeks," said the chief dealer at one large bank.
"Judging by the mood, it is likely to continue," he added.

Opposition leader Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa told Reuters in a recent interview that his Social Democrat party would not prevent the budget of the minority Socialist government passing in parliament if the alternative were fresh elections.

The budget, which will set a 2.9 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) budget deficit target for next year, down from a predicted four percent in 1996, is expected to be voted on in parliament in November.
To qualify for monetary union, candidate countries must cut their deficits to below three percent as well as meet targets for inflation and the state debt.
Other dealers also pointed to the influence of stop-loss orders as well as the interest rate differential with Germany as factors in the Portuguese currency's advance.
Portugal's interest rates in real terms are amongst the highest in Europe which makes them attractive if the exchange rate risk is seen as diminishing, analysts said.
The strength of the escudo could also be a reflection of the rise of the local bond market, they added.
"One thing is certain, with the mark-escudo at these levels, the Bank of Portugal can cut rates whenever it wants," said Basilio Leal of Banco Internacional do Funchal (Banif).
The Bank of Portugal will announce money market terms for the coming commercial bank reserve period on Thursday.
--Lisbon bureau 3511-3113121
